subject: Urgent: NovaHealth v4.2 quant rollout causing latency and 500s
messages:
From: Charlotte Lee <charlotte.lee@novahealth.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: samuel.park@novahealth.com
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 09:04:12 -0700
Subject: High latency + 500s after v4.2 quant profile - critical

Hi Vivek / Monica,

We pushed Redwood v4.2 (quant profile) to production at 03:15 PT and immediately started seeing P95 jump from ~250ms to ~800ms and a sustained 4xx/5xx spike (~6% of requests returning 500-like errors). Throughput dropped ~40% on our hot paths. This is impacting checkout flows and we have customers reporting timeouts.

We rolled a small traffic slice back to v4.1 and saw immediate improvement on that slice — P95 back to ~260ms and errors down. We need a plan: either full rollback or hotfix. Our CTO (cc'd) wants a call with your engineering lead + our SREs ASAP to understand root cause and a timeline for rollback.

I've attached a short metrics export from our side (metrics_snapshot_may17.csv). Please let me know availability in the next 30–60 minutes.

Thanks,
Charlotte
Charlotte Lee
Head of Platform Operations, NovaHealth
charlotte.lee@novahealth.com

Plan (first-pass):
- Immediate canary rollback of quant profile for 10% traffic (to confirm improvement end-to-end)
- If canary matches your observation, proceed to full rollback across the cluster (target: 30–45 mins)
- Parallel: capture KV cache traces and model runtime profiles for v4.2 vs v4.1

Looping in engineering leads (cc). Monica — can you confirm whether NovaHealth needs us to coordinate a maintenance window, or can we do a rolling change?

I'll join any call you open.

— Vivek

Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 09:35:10 -07:00
Subject: NOVA: urgent - v4.2 quant rollout causing p95/500s spike (customer-facing)

Team — Charlotte reported a clear regression after the v4.2 quant profile. NovaHealth sees P95 x3 and 4xx/5xx uptick; their canary to v4.1 fixed the slice. We need a quick decision: canary rollback now and if confirmed fast-follow to full rollback.

Immediate asks:
- Evelyn: please confirm whether this looks like a backend kernel/attention path regress (we saw similar when a kernel change changed tokenization micro-op ordering). Attach a rollback patch we can apply if needed.
- Marcus: prepare a rollout plan + playbook we can run with their SREs (step-by-step, rollback, smoke checks).
- Monica: coordinate customer comms and the call; get CTO on the line.

I attached a candidate rollback patch we can push to staging and then prod if green. If you don't have time for deep triage, do the rollback and we will post-mortem.

Attachments: redwood_rollback_patch_v4.1.patch (text, 12KB)

Time is sensitive — please respond with ETA for canary rollback.

— Vivek
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 10:12:33 -07:00
Subject: Re: NOVA: urgent - v4.2 quant rollout causing p95/500s spike (customer-facing)

Quick triage notes:
- I pulled recent runtime traces (sample attached). There's a clear increase in kernel launch overhead for the quantized attention path at sequence lengths typical for NovaHealth payloads (avg seq ~512). That combined with a new fused-kv cache write in v4.2 looks like it's causing tail latency amplification under high concurrency.
- The error class is primarily internal decoder OOM / timeout cascades (500s) when the runtime fails to allocate a short-lived temp buffer and then the request times out.

Recommendation: immediate canary rollback to v4.1 quant profile for 10% traffic. If the canary matches Charlotte's delta, then proceed to full rollback. I'll be available to monitor metrics and provide a hotfix branch if we want to keep v4.2 features but with the old kernel path.

Attached: quick_trace_snippet.txt (log excerpt, 8KB)

Eve
Evelyn Hart

Subject: Proposed immediate action: canary rollback then full rollback if validated

Charlotte / Samuel — thanks again for flagging. Summary and proposed immediate action: 

Summary: NovaHealth saw P95 jump and a 4–7% 500-level error rate after Redwood v4.2 quant profile was applied. Engineering analysis suggests a kernel-level latency amplification and temporary allocation failure under your workload patterns.

Proposed action (we can execute within 30–45 minutes):
1) Canary rollback: move 10% of traffic back to v4.1 quant profile, monitor 15 minutes for P95, error rate, and throughput.
2) If canary shows expected improvement, perform full rollback across all regions (target: additional 15–30 minutes).
3) Post-rollback: we will run a controlled experiment on a replica cluster to reproduce and isolate the kernel regression; provide an exec summary and patch timeline by EOD tomorrow.

Do we have permission to run the canary now? If you prefer a scheduled maintenance window, please propose a time.

We've opened an internal incident: INC-1842 (link below) and attached the minimal rollback patch for engineering review.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
